# Phase 5b — Throughput

Engineering note for `roadmap.md` Phase 5, second half. **D1, re-expressed 2026-09-28 as a
budget:** High profile, any picture up to 1,620 macroblocks, real time up to **97,200
macroblocks a second** (854x480p60; 720x480p60 is 81,000, 640x480p60 72,000) at the
bitrate of a Moonlight session requesting 10 Mbit/s. In cosim cycles at clk_dec 96.43 MHz,
less the rig's 4-7 % under the DDR model: **97,200 → ≤ ~930 cycles a macroblock;
81,000 → ≤ ~1,110** (met: 1,084 after the streaming start, §5). The original gate (≤ ~935
at 81 MHz, 720x480p60) is kept in the tables below for its history. Measured on the
Sunshine-shaped NVENC proxy at 8 Mbit/s at the encoder (`sun_high_8M`), then real time on
the rig from a live session. Status at the end (§6).

**The remaining levers, estimated from the 96.43 MHz profile after the streaming start**
(1,084 a macroblock: `M_INTER_WAIT` 566, the residual wait / add 78 + 65, the input wait
58, save + side data + deblock hand-off ~120, intra ~80, motion read ~27):

| lever | what it cuts | estimate | cost / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4b. two samples a cycle out of `mc_interp` (and wpred, pbuf0, the sample-bank write two bytes wide) | the interpolation (`K_WEIGHT_WAIT` 537: a whole-fractional 16x16 luma is 452 reads at one a cycle) | **-150 to -200** (then the fetch's own rate binds: 4 bytes a cycle copied, DDR at 90 MHz) | the largest change: mc_interp's sweep and filters doubled; `run_mc.sh` is bit-exact over every class, so the risk is effort, not correctness |
| 4c. the next macroblock's inter under this one's tail | the serial tail (residual add, save, deblock hand-off ~200) overlapped with the next fetch / sweep | -50 to -150 | recon_mb's control: the next macroblock's motion early, a second prediction bank; the riskiest in control |
| 5. the front end (UMD's deferred `mb_syntax` issue / emit merge) | the input wait (`M_IDLE` 58 at 8 Mbit/s, 150 at 12) | -20 to -40 at 8 Mbit/s, more at higher rates | ported from UMD's design |
| residual add | `M_RES_ADD_RD` 65 (the sample RAM read per 4x4) | -20 to -40 | small |
| the clock to 101.25 MHz (VCO 810 / 8) | +5 % across the board | ≈ -50 equivalent | a fit gate of ~106 at both corners: another retime round from a 101.46 fit with no margin |
| (the back engine: deblock + writeback, ~740 busy) | -- | binds only once the front is under ~750 | -- |

Needed for 97,200: ~-155 (1,084 → ~930). **4b alone probably reaches it; 4b + 5 gives
margin.** **Decided 2026-09-28 (the maintainer): the gate is 81,000 (720x480p60) now** --
met in the model, the rig confirms it; 97,200 is 4b's target and becomes the gate once 4b
is measured.

## 2. Where the cycles go (2026-09-28, the merged P5a netlist, 81 MHz)

recon_mb's front, cycles a macroblock:

| window | total | inter wait | residual wait (`M_RES_NEXT`) | deblock hand-off (`M_DB_WAIT`) | input wait (`M_IDLE`) | residual add | save + side | intra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sun_high_8M` | **1,218** | 636 | 115 | 100 | 44 | 56 + 24 | 55 | ~80 |
| `sun_high_12M` | 1,388 | 574 | 182 | 100 | 150 | 71 + 24 | 55 | ~120 |
| `sun_main_8M` | 1,214 | 649 | 109 | 100 | 49 | 56 + 24 | 55 | ~70 |
| `x264_sunh` | 1,255 | 605 | 112 | 100 | 30 | 56 + 24 | 55 | ~150 |
| `cap_10000` | 986 | 631 | 38 | 100 | 20 | 24 + 24 | 55 | ~10 |

Inside the inter wait: the interpolation side (`K_WEIGHT_WAIT` ~400-455) runs **one sample
a cycle** -- `mc_interp` is bound by its 8-bit window read port (a fractional 16x16 reads
(w+5)(h+5) = 441 bytes: 452 cycles; `mc_interp.sv`'s header table) -- and the fetch side
(`I_FETCH` ~300-360) overlaps it per item through the double-buffered window. The residual
engine (`R_FEED` 490-665 busy) is the second serial unit: one coefficient a cycle into
`dequant_itrans`, one block at a time. The deblock hand-off is a flat 100: the bS pre-pass
takes 3 cycles for each of 32 edge groups (`recon_deblock.sv` `D_PRE`), and the front
waits for it (`M_DB_WAIT`) because the end walk rewrites the records it reads.

## 3. The levers, and the plan

Measured cost first, largest-per-effort first:

1. **The deblock pre-pass: ~-65 on every macroblock.** One group a cycle (the q and p
   records from two copies of the record RAM, or a pipelined single port) instead of three:
   ~35 cycles. No format risk; `run_recon_top.sh` / `run_deblock.sh` gate it.
2. **The clock.** 81 MHz is inherited (MiSTer_DVD chose it for MPEG-2; UMD kept it for
   Level 3.0, `sys_pll.sv`), not a device or format limit. What limits clk_dec is the fit:
   it must close ~5 MHz above the running clock at both slow corners (MiSTer_DVD's fits at
   81-83 misbehaved on hardware: `fmax_check.sh`). The P5a fit closes 87.4 at -40 C.
   `clk_mem` stays at 90 (the f2sdram bridge's measured ceiling; clk_dec already crosses
   to it through FIFOs). Timing of the P5a fit re-analysed at higher targets
   (`timing_paths.sh`, -40 C): the paths failing a 95 / 105 MHz gate sit in **four modules**
   -- `intra_pred`, `mv_pred`, `dequant_itrans` (4x4), `recon_dpb` -- plus a few dozen in
   `recon_inter`'s row-buffer LUT-RAM reads and `mb_syntax`; the CABAC engine has ~10 at
   105. At 100 MHz the D1 budget is ~1,154 cycles a macroblock (935 x 100 / 81); the DDR
   round trips do not shrink (clk_mem is unchanged), so the fetch part scales less than
   linearly -- measured, not assumed, once the clock moves (the cosim models clk_mem
   separately).
3. **The residual engine: `M_RES_NEXT` 115-182.** The front waits for blocks the engine has
   not transformed yet. The engine feeds a block, then waits for its LAST output sample
   before the next one's setup: ~45 cycles a coded 4x4 block, ~900 for a fully coded inter
   macroblock -- longer than the inter prediction it hides behind. `dequant_itrans` is built
   to take the next block as soon as `busy` drops (its intake overlapping the previous
   block's output: 27 cycles a block steady, its header), so: a feed side that starts on
   `!busy`, a collector that writes each block's samples from a small descriptor FIFO, the
   serial wait kept only around the DC blocks (their outputs feed the next blocks' R_DC)
   and the 8x8 unit (no overlap, and it shares the result muxes).
4. **The inter floor: ~600.** (The 96.43 MHz profile, §5, splits it: the first window's
   fetch ~200 by difference, then the interpolation ~454.) The original text: Two samples a cycle out of `mc_interp` (a 16-bit window read:
   the window RAM is already four byte lanes) halves `K_WEIGHT_WAIT`; the fetch must then
   keep up (it overlaps today at ~300-360 a macroblock). The largest change; after 1-3 are
   measured.
5. **The front end above ~8 Mbit/s** (`M_IDLE` 44 → 150 at 12 Mbit/s): UMD's deferred
   `mb_syntax` issue / emit merge. For the "higher rates decode correctly and fall behind
   visibly" half of D1, not its gate.

6. **The back engine (~800 a macroblock busy: `E_DB` ~400, the writeback ~400 of which ~160
   is five setup states a row).** Overlapped with the front today; it becomes the wall once
   the front drops under ~800 (`M_DB_GO` waits for it).

Margin: UMD measured the rig 4-7 % slower than the cosim's DDR model, so the target in the
cosim is ~10 % under the budget (≤ ~1,040 at 100 MHz), confirmed on the rig with a live
session at the end.

## 4. Decisions to take with the maintainer

- **The PLL's reachable clocks.** outclk_3 shares the VCO with 27 MHz (pixel) and 90 MHz (the
  DDR3 bridge), so exactly 100 is out (a 2,700 MHz VCO). Near it: **96.43 MHz** (VCO 1,350,
  / 14; 27 = / 50, 90 = / 15) and **101.25 MHz** (VCO 810, / 8; today's VCO). Endpoints
  failing each fit gate on `d6e7b69` (`TIMING_BELOW`, one path per endpoint, -40 C): a
  96 MHz gate ~170 (recon_dpb 125, recon_mb 49); **a 101 gate ~630** (recon_dpb 279,
  recon_mb 115, mb_syntax 83, mv_pred 28, cabac 19, sps_pps 18, wpred 10, dequant 8, ...);
  a 106 gate ~1,670 across ~20 modules (the parser's control logic included). **Target:
  96.43 MHz** (budget 1,113 cycles a macroblock at D1's margin; `sun_high_8M` ~1,155 there
  today: the inter widening closes it); 101.25 only if the 96.43 fit ends with room.
- The clock: **decided 2026-09-28 with the maintainer: aim for ~100 MHz** (a fit ~5 MHz
  above the clock at both slow corners), validated on the rig; the inter prediction widened
  next for the margin the rig's 4-7 % needs. **Done in the RTL:** `sys_pll` outclk_3 =
  **96.428571 MHz** (VCO 1,350: M 27, N 1; 27 = / 50, 90 = / 15, the unused outclk_2 now
  25 = / 54), `tools/fmax_check.sh` FMAX_MIN **101.4** (96.43 + MiSTer_DVD's 5 MHz),
  `recon_dpb`'s STALL_LIMIT rescaled (13 M cycles, ~135 ms, the same ~4 frame periods),
  the cosim's default clock 96.43 (`+clk_khz=N` / `+clk_mhz=N` for others). The rig must
  still confirm the 5 MHz rule holds at this clock.
- **The retime campaign** (-40 C fits of each batch, §5): 87.37 (P5a) → 80.22 (intra_pred's
  state-selected tap index: a static path, not placement) → 86.78 → 89.06 → 90.02 → 86.49
  (a fit with no longer path than the one before: ±3 MHz is placement at 65 % ALM, so a
  batch is judged by the endpoint census under the target, not one fmax) → **94.49**
  (`3b00642`: 73 endpoints left under the 101 gate). The pattern in almost every fix: a
  **wide compare or lookup whose result fans out to many loads in the same cycle**
  (a POC compare behind a 20-way store select, a range check on a parsed value, a DSP
  product in front of a position test) -- registered one cycle early, or moved to a
  cycle where its inputs are already settled (the mvd mask on the x word, the geometry
  one position ahead, the rLPS row stored beside the CABAC state). Per-picture and
  per-slice logic (the DPB, the parsers) was the bulk of it, not the macroblock loop.

**At 96.43 MHz** (`35fbe54` + the window-scan retime, the cosim's new default clock,
`sun_high_8M` 120 frames, `+prof`): **1,168 cycles a macroblock = 61.1 frames/s, 1.01x real
time** -- past 60 in the model, not past the rig's 4-7 %. `M_INTER_WAIT` 667 of it.
Reading the inter histograms takes care: `I_LIST` (185) is the fetch WAITING for a free
window bank (the interpolator still on the item before) and `I_DRAIN` (77) waiting for the
interpolator to finish -- interpolator time seen from the fetch side, not fetch work; and
`I_IDLE` 503 / `K_IDLE` 698 are mostly recon_inter idle between macroblocks. The chain a
macroblock waits on is: **the first window's fetch** (the interpolator has nothing yet:
~200 by difference, not yet measured directly: DDR round trips at 90 MHz, one row command
each) **then the interpolation**
(`K_WEIGHT_WAIT` 454: a whole-fractional 16x16 luma 452 is most of it, the chroma behind
it), the later windows' fetches hidden behind it. Both halves are levers: two samples a
cycle out of `mc_interp` (lever 4 as written) shortens the second; starting a
macroblock's first fetch earlier (under the previous macroblock's residual / deblock
hand-off, once its motion is known) hides the first. Measured before designing -- the
advisor's point, and the reason the widening waited for this profile.

**The streaming start** (lever 4a, 2026-09-28): an item's interpolation starts while its
window is still arriving -- recon_inter claims the bank with its descriptor at the fetch's
start and counts each row the edge its last byte lands (`bank_rows`); `mc_interp` reads a
row only once counted (`rows_avail`). `sun_high_8M` at 96.43 MHz: **1,168 → 1,084 cycles
a macroblock = 65.9 frames/s, 1.09x real time**, bit-exact over the 120 frames.
`M_INTER_WAIT` 667 → 566; `I_LIST` (the fetch waiting on a claimed bank) 185 → 79;
`K_WEIGHT_WAIT` 454 → 537 (the interpolation now includes the time it follows the fetch:
the fetch and the sweep overlap instead of adding). Gates: `run_mc.sh` `+rows=1` (rows
released one by one, unreleased rows X; M11 the gate removed, caught only there),
`run_recon_top.sh` T5 / T6. Cost: 5 + 2 x 5 registers and a 5-bit compare on `issue`.

**Two interpolation lanes** (lever 4b, 2026-09-28): a partition 8 or more wide in its plane
is swept by two `mc_interp` copies over its column halves (lane 1 at `col_off` = w/2 of
the same window, the whole window's `win_stride`), each with its own window-RAM copy,
list-0 buffer, prefetch and `wpred`; each lane hands its row segment (4 or 8 samples,
always inside one sample-RAM word) over as one byte-enabled word write, the two sharing
the port through a one-deep pending register each. Luma 4 and chroma 4 / 2 stay on lane 0.
`sun_high_8M` at 96.43 MHz: **1,084 → 1,035 cycles a macroblock = 69.0 frames/s, 1.14x
real time**, bit-exact; `x264_film` 915. Less than the -150..-200 estimated, and the
profile says why: `K_WEIGHT_WAIT` 537 → 435 only, because with the streaming start the
sweep follows the FETCH, which is now the wall (`I_FETCH` 404); and `M_DB_GO` 28 → 57 --
the back engine (deblock + writeback, ~744 busy) starts to be waited on.

**Where the fetch goes** (a scratch cosim classifying each `I_FETCH` cycle, the same run):

| class | cycles a macroblock |
|---|---|
| **requests out, no data yet (the DDR round trip)** | **245** |
| receiving beats | 111 |
| the copy's tail (all received) | 40 |
| a row command waiting for the port / nothing requested ahead | 8 |

The fetch is LATENCY-bound, not bandwidth-bound: inside one window 16 rows are in flight,
but at every item boundary (Y, Cb, Cr, each list of a bi-predicted group) the request side
waits for the whole window to arrive and be copied (`cp_row == wh_q`, then `I_LIST` ..
`I_LIST4`) before the next window's first row is requested -- every item pays a full
round trip. **Next (4c'): requests that run ahead into the next item** -- the per-item
geometry pipelined a stage ahead of the copy, the row buffers tagged by item, the copy
still waiting for a free window bank. Worth up to ~150-200 of the 245. Then the back
engine (`M_DB_GO`).

**The fetch run-ahead** (lever 4c', 2026-09-28): the fetch in three sides. REQUEST walks the
items and issues each window's rows, pushing the item into a two-entry queue as its
requests start and going straight on to the next item (bounded by the queue and the
sixteen row buffers, now a ring indexed by global row counts); RECEIVE follows the queue's
items into the ring; COPY claims a free window bank for the oldest item (the descriptor:
the streaming start is kept), copies, pops. Each side latches its item's geometry at its
start, so the queue adds no mux to the copy's retimed address path. `sun_high_8M` at 96.43
MHz: **1,035 → 990 cycles a macroblock = 72.2 frames/s, 1.19x real time**, bit-exact
(`I_REQ` 154 where `I_FETCH` was 404). The recon_top clips pass against three DDR models
(default; fast 1-2 mclk, no waitrequest; slow 20-60 mclk, 60 % waitrequest). New arm T9 (a
bank claimed while still in use: caught under the fast model); the stage-0 copy of the
item's first word and a 17-row bound are equivalent by construction (the claim is a cycle
after the pop; the ring's full flags are the correctness, the bound is flow) -- the
first removed, both documented.

Where it stands: the deblock / writeback engine is busy ~772 a macroblock and waited on
63 (`M_DB_GO`); 97,200 macroblocks/s needs <= ~930 in the cosim: ~60 to go. Candidates:
the macroblock's first window under the previous macroblock's tail (4c), the residual
wait / add (98 + 65), the back engine's writeback setup (`E_CMD` .. `E_NEXT`, ~160).

**The writeback's row setup overlapped** (2026-09-28): the back engine walked five serial
states a writeback row (E_NEXT, E_CMD, E_ADDR, E_ADDR2, E_ISSUE: ~160 cycles a macroblock)
before each row's words. E_ISSUE now steps `wb_row` to the next row while latching the
current one for the data phase (`d_row` / `d_plane`), and E_DATA refreshes the next row's
position every cycle, so the address pipeline has it ready when the words are out (three
edges; a row's data takes at least four cycles): only an item's first row still walks
E_CMD .. E_ADDR2. `sun_high_8M`: **990 → 968 cycles a macroblock = 73.8 frames/s, 1.22x**,
bit-exact; the back engine busy ~772 → ~679, `M_DB_GO` 63 → 30. Its words are still one
at a time (a read, two edges of latency, the push: `E_DATA` 310) -- the next back-engine
lever if it binds again.

**On the rig** (2026-09-28, `3ec031c`, `history.md` §6): `sun854_high_8M` (854x480p60, 8
Mbit/s at the encoder) 300 / 300, late 0, starved 0, the decoder idle 0.9 % -- 97,200
macroblocks a second real time on hardware, ~1 % to spare; `sun854_high_5M` idle 7.1 %;
`sun_high_8M` (720x480p60) idle 13.0 %. The cosim criterion (<= ~930 on `sun_high_8M`) is
not reached (968); the last levers (§ the table at the top) stay open behind the display
work, the maintainer's order (2026-09-28).

**854x480p60 by bitrate** (2026-09-28, the fetch run-ahead's tree; the maintainer asked
whether a lower bitrate makes it real time already): the same NVENC recipe as the proxies
(High, p1 ull CBR, a one-frame VBV, refs 1, 1 slice) from the same film source cropped to
16:9 and scaled to 854x480 (coded 864x480 cropped, 1,620 macroblocks), `.sim/p5b/`
(`sun854_high_{3,5,8}M.264`, gitignored), 120 frames, every picture exact:

| at the encoder | cycles a macroblock | frames/s at 96.43 MHz | cosim real time | the rig (4-7 % under) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 Mbit/s | 851 | 69.9 | 1.16x | ~1.08-1.12x |
| 5 Mbit/s | 896 | 66.4 | 1.10x | ~1.03-1.06x |
| 8 Mbit/s | 949 | 62.7 | 1.04x | ~0.97-1.00x: borderline |

A macroblock costs less at 854 wide than at 720 for the same bitrate (949 vs 990 at 8
Mbit/s: the bits spread over 20 % more macroblocks). So 854x480p60 is real time up to ~5
Mbit/s at the encoder (a ~6-7 Mbit/s request) on this tree; the last ~60 cycles a
macroblock are what 8 Mbit/s (a 10 Mbit/s request) needs. Not rig-measured yet, and not
watchable yet: the display does not fit a picture wider than 720 to the raster.

**The clock, measured** (2026-09-28, `d6e7b69`, `sun_high_8M`, the cosim's `+clk_mhz=N`: clk_dec
at N MHz, the DDR3 bridge held at 90): 81 MHz 1,132 cycles a macroblock = 53.0 frames/s;
90 MHz 1,147 = 58.1; **100 MHz 1,162 = 63.7 frames/s** -- D1's gate (935 at 81 = 64.2 frames/s)
reached within 1 %. The cycles rise only ~1.4 % per 10 MHz: the DDR-latency-bound fetch is
a small share of the critical path, so the clock scales nearly linearly. The rig's 4-7 %
under the DDR model means the clock alone is AT the gate, not past it.

## 7. The headroom clock: 103.85 MHz (✅ MERGED, PR fj#17; ✅ HW-CONFIRMED, 2026-09-30; reverted to 96.43 by PR fj#22)

> **Superseded (2026-10-01, PR fj#22):** the macroblock pipeline gives D1 ~1.4x at 96.43 MHz, and at
> its 83 % ALM no seed closed 103.85's 108.8 gate; clk_dec is 96.43 again (gate 101.4,
> `mb_pipeline.md` §4f). What follows is the record of the 103.85 work.

**Why.** 854x480p60 at a 10 Mbit/s request ran real time on the rig with ~1 % to spare
(§5, `history.md` §6): a busier scene falls behind, and Phase 6b's overlay fetch takes ram2
time out of that same margin (`architecture.md` Phase 6b: 16 bpp fits at ~0.9 %, 32 bpp would
not). The clock is the lever with no area: throughput scales ~linearly with it (§5, "the
clock, measured").

**The reachable clocks** (outclk_3 shares the VCO with 27 and 90 MHz, both kept exact):

| VCO | clk_dec | gain | fit gate (+5 MHz) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,350 | / 14 = 96.43 (P5b) | -- | 101.4 |
| 1,080 | / 11 = 98.18 | +1.8 % | 103.2 |
| 810 | / 8 = 101.25 | +5.0 % | 106.25 |
| **1,350** | **/ 13 = 103.85** | **+7.7 %** | **108.8** |
| 1,080 | / 10 = 108.0 | +12 % | 113 |

**Chosen: 103.85 MHz** (with the maintainer, 2026-09-30: "raise clk_dec to ~102-103"). The
census on the pad-home netlist (constrained at 96.43, fitted 109.59 / 108.46) had 3-4 endpoints
per corner under a 108.85 gate and one failing; the next step, 108 MHz, had ~50+ under a 113
gate at -40 C alone (a retime campaign, not a round). What moved with it: `sys_pll` outclk_3
(`103.846153 MHz`, the fit's PLL summary confirms VCO 1,350 / 13), `fmax_check.sh` /
`seed_sweep.sh` FMAX_MIN 108.8, `recon_dpb`'s STALL_LIMIT 14 M (~135 ms, unchanged in time),
the cosim's default clock, `h264.sdc`'s note (clk_dec / clk_sys now 0.74 ns apart at worst:
gcd(13, 50) = 1).

**The rounds** (the P5b playbook, `hw_budget_and_lessons.md` §5):

| fit | clk_dec 100 C / -40 C | census under 108.8 | fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `879fc91` (the clock alone) | 105.8 / 104.23 | 13 / 12 endpoints, four clusters | `recon_dpb` frame_num's wrap test registered at the opening (per picture); `slice_hdr` SliceQPY's check behind `f_val` (per slice); `mb_syntax`'s neighbour tables split by consumer (the cbf copy indexed by `rb_idx`, no state compare); `sfifo`'s `rd_ok` / `full` from register-only predicates |
| `c63a195` | 106.6 / 109.59 | 7 / 0 (hot only), one cluster | `recon_lists` L_FIELD's parity registered in phase 0 beside `f_stn` |
| `7340353` | 102.3 / 102.92 (**negative slack at 103.85**) | 47 at 100 C, one cluster | `recon_dpb` D_POC1_RD2's two dependent 32-bit compare-and-subtracts (the non-reference decrement, the divider's -1): met before, moved by round 2's placement -- split into D_POC1_RD3 (one cycle a picture) |
| `e125f75` | 106.92 / 107.81 | 19 / 7, spread: `recon_lists` `lw_d` again (11, from `cent` now), `recon_hdr` `h_delta_poc0` (8), `mv_pred` `t2_py` -> RAM (5) | a seed sweep of this netlist (placement, not a path: each fix moves the next cluster) |
| `e125f75`, **SEED 9** (the sweep's first seed) | **111.77 / 110.41** | -- | **PASS at both corners**; ALM 32,469 (77 %), M10K 341, DSP 95 (`H264_clkup_20260930_2013.rbf`) |

None of the fixes adds a cycle: the two predicates are registered in states that already wait,
the table split and the sfifo predicates change nothing the design does. Each new register stage
has an arm (`run_recon_ctl.sh` D7 / L4; `run_h264_top.sh` S2 already reaches `p_qp`;
`run_dpb_mem.sh` F3 / F4 for sfifo's `full`, F4 needing a new `sfifo_tb` phase: a `full` that
clears a cycle late loses nothing and costs one refused push each time the RAM tops out).

**On the rig** (`history.md` §16): `sun854_high_8M` -- 854x480p60 at a ~10 Mbit/s request, D1's
hardest case -- the decoder idle 5.9 % (0.9 % at 96.43), ~1.06x real time; `sun854_high_5M`
11.6 % (7.1 %), `sun_high_8M` 17.7 % (13.0 %); every picture, errors 0, late 0, starved 0.
The gain is ~4.6-5 points of idle, under the clock's +7.7 %: the reference fetch is
DDR3-latency bound and clk_mem stays at 90, so each further MHz of clk_dec returns less (a
108 MHz step would buy less than its +4 %; the fetch, not the clock, is then the lever).
The cosim at 103.85 (`e125f75`, 120 frames, every picture bit-exact; `run_cosim.sh --sweep
--dir .sim/p5b`): `sun854_high_3M` 840 cycles a macroblock (851 at 96.43, §5's table), 1.26x;
`sun854_high_5M` 885 (896), 1.20x; `sun854_high_8M` 941 (949), **1.13x**; `sun_high_8M` 985
(968), 1.29x. Cycles a macroblock barely move with the clock (the DDR3 round trips cost more
clk_dec cycles at 103.85, the retimes added none) -- the frames a second scale with it.
Pre-merge gates on `e125f75`: `run_recon_top.sh` 40 / 40, `run_cosim.sh` GREEN (every window
bit-exact), `run_mb_syntax.sh --red` / `run_h264_top.sh --red` / `run_recon_ctl.sh --red` /
`run_dpb_mem.sh --red` ALL GREEN, `run_aud_play.sh` GREEN.

**Known, not fixed here: `dec_stub`'s reset recovery.** Every fit's timing report shows negative
*recovery* slack into clk_dec (worst -1.755 ns on the merged pad-home build at 96.43; -2.4 ns at
103.85, where clk_dec / clk_sys edges are 0.74 ns apart): the 24-bit heartbeat counter in
`h264/dec_stub.sv` is cleared asynchronously by `reset_n` (clk_sys: `user_rst_q`, the OSD Reset)
and released with no synchroniser -- by its own comment "treated as async here". The one clk_dec
reset that skips the `cdc_reset` rule; the decoder's own (`fe_rst_cdc`, `dec_lock_cdc`) meet
recovery with +1.3 ns. Harmless (a metastable release shifts the LED blink's phase, nothing
else reads the counter), and `fmax_check.sh` watches setup only, which is why it went unseen.
Fix (the next branch that fits anyway: any netlist change re-rolls the pinned seed): a
`cdc_reset` into clk_dec inside `dec_stub`, and a recovery check beside the setup gate.

**The plan if the clock does not close** (the maintainer, 2026-09-30): Phase 6b's overlay next
-- the last large logic addition -- then read what area is left before the four lanes (lever
4b's second step: ~+660 ALM, +9 M10K, +5 DSP a lane as measured at 4b, so ~+1,300 ALM, +18 M10K,
**+10 DSP** for two more: DSP 95 -> ~105 of 112 is the binding resource; and the lane's gain is
capped by the latency-bound fetch -- measure with a profile before paying the area).

**The margin rule stays 5 MHz** (asked 2026-09-30 whether it could be lowered at these clocks):
it is MiSTer_DVD's measurement, not a datasheet figure (its 81 MHz fits at 81-83 misbehaved on
hardware, a chroma fringe that followed the seed); a decoder carries a marginal flip forward in
its references until the next IDR, and nothing the rig reads today (the error counters, a
viewer) can see a slightly wrong pixel. Lowering it wants an instrument first: a checksum of
each decoded picture in the status block against a software decode of the same clip, run warm
for hours on a deliberately marginal build.

## 8. The 93 % ALM retime (`perf/retime`, 2026-10-13)

**Why.** From chroma reconstruction (2026-10-10, 93 % ALM) every RTL branch missed clk_dec's 101.4 MHz
gate on its first fit and needed a seed sweep -- interface 1.1's failed nine seeds before a second sweep found
one; `fix/chroma-field`'s missed SEEDs 1-4. Each change was small and far from the decoder; the seed moved
the decoder's own placement, and fits landed 96-103 MHz either side of the gate. Decided with the maintainer
(2026-10-13): retime the decoder's paths, the `hw_budget_and_lessons.md` §5 playbook, aiming at ~105 MHz on a
first roll.

**The census** (every endpoint below 105 MHz -- slack 0.846 ns at the 96.43 MHz constraint -- at both slow
corners) on main's netlist at three seeds:

| path | SEED 5 (-40 / 100) | SEED 4 | SEED 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| recon_top: `sz_prod` (w x h) -> the 3,600 compare -> `ref_size` / the hand-off | 15 / 50 | 16 / 16 | -- |
| mc_interp: `fy_7` -> Table 8-12's select -> the average -> `fmem`'s write | 6 / 8 | 15 / 8 | -- |
| recon_hdr: the FIFO's word -> the router -> the field decode | 2 / -- | -- / 8 | 11 / 16 |
| recon_inter: `kb` -> `tgt` / `q_n` / `wt_addr` | 3 / -- | -- / 7 | 1 / 3 |
| mv_pred: `dec_done` -> `nb_sel_q`; `t2_py` -> the motion RAM | -- | 1 / 1 | 14 / 10 |
| intra_pred, mb_intake, recon_mb (`r_blk` -> `dc_nz`), recon_lists, recon_dpb | 2-4 each | 5-9 | 1-3 |

Different seeds, different clusters: placement. The fixes went to the paths present on most seeds.

**Round 1** (`a7a3bf1`): recon_top's size check in three registered steps (the sides, the product, the
compare; recon_dpb takes the slice at `sr_d3`, two cycles a slice); mc_interp's S8 (Table 8-12's operands
registered, the average and the FIFO write a stage later -- the output credits bound every sample in flight, so
no flow-control change, every case still inside `LAT_MAX`); recon_inter's lane sample count registered per bank
from its own descriptor; the header words and `hdr_end` registered into recon_hdr (a word registered as `clear`
arrives is dropped). Benches: `run_recon_top.sh --red` ALL GREEN (95 mutations, S4-S6 re-anchored, S7 new),
`run_mc.sh --red` (M16 new). **Fit SEED 5 first roll 103.22 / 102.17 PASS**; census 16 / 15 endpoints. ALUTs
+276, registers +229; the size product now maps to a 9x9 DSP (110 of 112).

**Round 2** (`69cc881`): the two clusters left -- recon_mb's QPY and chroma QPs in two registered steps (settled
by `A_QP`: the fields hold from `A_IDLE` through four load states), recon_inter's setup target's fields latched as
the setup leaves `KS_IDLE` (one bank for the whole sequence; a claimed bank's descriptor holds). T13 / T14.

**Round 2's seeds.** SEED 5 had passed first roll (104.2 / 103.21), but SEEDs 1 / 2 / 4 of the same netlist fitted
93.08 / 96.83 / 99.93 (cold corner): the spread unchanged. Their censuses named the clusters round 3 took.

**Round 3** (`88235c8`): mv_pred's 10:1 entry mux selected without `dec_done` (D whenever C is inside the macroblock:
if C is available there the entry is internal and `nb_sel_q` unused; SEED 1 had 51 / 44 endpoints, negative); mb_intake's
slot-use table registered from the layout's next values (equal on every cycle); recon_mb's uncoded-DC clears written
from `r_blk` and its coded bit (the skip branch is taken for a DC block exactly when it is not coded). M23 / I14 / T15.
Seeds 5 / 1 / 2 / 4: 93.37 / 101.0 / 100.53 / 94.23 -- again the same spread, the clusters elsewhere.

**The fitter's target** (`h264/h264_fit.sdc`, `a1cb7d4`): Quartus' Auto Fit eases off once a clock's constraint is
met, and clk_dec's is its real 96.43 MHz -- nothing asked the fitter for the gate's 101.4. 0.8 ns of extra setup
uncertainty into clk_dec while `quartus_fit` runs (`quartus_sta`, the gate's report, never reads it) makes it aim at
~104.5 MHz. Its own file, after `sys/sys.qip` in the qsf: `sys_top.sdc` derives the PLL clocks, and in `h264.sdc` (read
first) the command matched no clock and was ignored -- the first try's fit identical to the bit. Round 3 with it:
seeds 5 / 1 / 2 / 4 = 99.21 / **102.79 (102.28 at 100 C) PASS** / 99.26 / 96.79 -- about +2-3 MHz on average, the
spread a little narrower, still one seed in four.

| netlist (cold corner, MHz) | SEED 5 | SEED 1 | SEED 2 | SEED 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 102.18 | 97.82 | 96.40 | 98.63 |
| round 2 | 103.21 | 93.08 | 96.83 | 99.93 |
| round 3 | 93.37 | 101.0 | 100.53 | 94.23 |
| round 3 + `h264_fit.sdc` | 99.21 | **102.79** | 99.26 | 96.79 |

**The verdict** (decided with the maintainer 2026-10-13: merge as is): at 93-98 % ALM placement decides; a retime moves
which paths fail, not the seed spread -- the playbook's stop rule (`hw_budget_and_lessons.md` §5, "stop when the census
stops being one cluster") was met at round 2. Kept: the three rounds (bit-exact, each fix a real census cluster, no
throughput cost) and the fitter's target; a sweep stays part of each RTL branch. **Not taken:** clk_dec lowered to ~90
MHz (most seeds would pass; ~7 % throughput: 720p30 8 Mbit/s ~1.13x -> ~1.05x), and freeing logic (a project of its own).

**On .201** (SEED 1, `H264_retimeoc_20261013_0846.rbf`), main's build (`H264_chromafieldsweep_20261013_0155.rbf`) the
control arm, `h264play` with VUI pacing, idle = `rc_stall` over the pictures' play time at 96.43 MHz: the 10 Mbit/s
Sunshine capture (1,315 pictures) idle 64.8 % on both; x264 720p30 8 Mbit/s (testsrc2 + noise, 600 pictures) idle
17.5 % on both (1.21x) -- every picture, errors / late 0. The retime's added cycles (two a slice, one of mc_interp's
latency) do not show.

**Left alone:** mv_pred's temporal-direct stage (it writes the motion RAM at t2: a stage there moves the write against
the next reads) and the single-seed clusters (cabac_engine, dequant_itrans, recon_dpb's `drop_n`, recon_lists).
